summary:
Turn 54 closed the silent half of the durability call-site defect with a second scenario on the same obligation.

What was observed locally. With Durable true and the recovering replica's own row already holding a different instance at the same number (seeded with distinctive metadata: seq 0x33333333, status ACCEPTED), the real startPhase1 for the owner's instance records that other record: the stable store receives seq 858993459 — equal to the own row's seq and not the new instance's seq 0 — with the own row's ACCEPTED status, while the new instance is installed under the owner's row. So in the case where no panic occurs the log silently carries a different instance's ballot context, which completes the picture the previous artifact began with the nil-record case.

Product. A second artifact on the same unit (unit-C9-durable-recorder-uses-the-instance-row), claiming the same duty (the metadata recorded for a phase-1 write must belong to the instance being written) with a new plan and harness: a prerequisite event prints the durability flag and the own row's metadata, and the result asserts recorded_matches_new_instance == true, with instance identity correlation, the existing phase-1 binding and the same grounding. The plan records the decoding caveat honestly — the recorded bytes are read with the recorder's own layout, which claim C2 shows is not readable as documented — and that the durable path is inert in the shipped configuration.

Frontier. The C9 finding now has two scenarios (the crash on an absent record, reviewed, and this silent wrong-metadata write, awaiting the trusted runner and a fresh correspondence review), joining the C1 family as a multi-scenario obligation. Audit spec moved to version 12; the other seven settled claims, the two paused candidates and the scope-issue bookkeeping item are untouched, and no requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
